scenes.dialogue: On twenty eighth October, a Karnataka High Court bench of Honourable Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Honourable Justice K S Hemalekha ruled.
scenes.shown: On 28 October, a Karnataka High Court bench of Honourable Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Honourable Justice K.S. Hemalekha ruled.

scenes.dialogue: K M V Projects contracted with the State Project Director to build school buildings in Bidar. The works ran late, and its price escalation bills went unpaid.
scenes.shown: KMV Projects contracted with the State Project Director to build school buildings in Bidar. The works ran late, and its price escalation bills went unpaid.

scenes.dialogue: In arbitration, K M V was awarded about sixty one lakh rupees, with interest. But its escalation claim, over two crore rupees, was rejected.
scenes.shown: In arbitration, KMV was awarded about ₹61.6 lakh, with interest. But its escalation claim, over ₹2 crore, was rejected.

scenes.dialogue: The reason: the tender document K M V produced carried a note deleting the price adjustment clause. And K M V failed to prove the amount claimed.
scenes.shown: The reason: the tender document KMV produced carried a note deleting the price adjustment clause. And KMV failed to prove the amount claimed.

scenes.dialogue: Under Section Thirty Three, it said it had filed old, obsolete tender documents by mistake. The tribunal held that was no clerical error, and refused.
scenes.shown: Under Section 33, it said it had filed old, obsolete tender documents by mistake. The tribunal held that was no clerical error, and refused.

scenes.dialogue: Its Section Thirty Four petition failed. In appeal, K M V said it should have been allowed to file its revised tender, and the amount was undisputed.
scenes.shown: Its Section 34 petition failed. In appeal, KMV said it should have been allowed to file its revised tender, and the amount was undisputed.

scenes.dialogue: The High Court held: the award rested on K M V's own documents, which showed the clause deleted. Under Section Thirty Four's narrow scope, it can't be faulted.
scenes.shown: The High Court held: the award rested on KMV's own documents, which showed the clause deleted. Under Section 34's narrow scope, it can't be faulted.

scenes.dialogue: And even if the clause applied, K M V never showed how the claim was computed. It had to prove the measure, not just entitlement. The appeal was dismissed.
scenes.shown: And even if the clause applied, KMV never showed how the claim was computed. It had to prove the measure, not just entitlement. The appeal was dismissed.
